2 ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.IV, VIJAYAPUR, IN MVC NO.1791/2016.
 -3-  NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB  MFA No. 202229 of 2018 HC-KAR

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD  AND  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 14.09.2018 passed by the III-Addl.
District Judge and MACT-IV, in MVC No.1791/2016.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 18.02.2016 at 11.00 a.m., near Avarsa, Ankola, Uttarkannada, on NH-66, the driver of Swift dzire Car bearing No.MH-15/CM-0093 drove the same in rash and negligent manner, tried to overtake another vehicle, lost control over the car, dashed to the deceased Dundappa.

As a result of the aforesaid accident, NC:
2025:KHC-K:6564-DB HC-KAR the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased Dundappa along with interest.
4. On service of summons, respondent No.1 is placed ex-parte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.1 wife of the deceased as PW-1 and one eyewitness as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
On the other hand, respondents did not choose to adduce any evidence on their behalf but got exhibited one document namely insurance policy as Ex.R1.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia

, held that the accident took place on account of NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB Mangala W/O Dundappa @ Gundappa ... vs Swati W/O Subhash Babhulagaonkar And ... on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112153036/
3 HC-KAR rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.9,92,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
and directed the respondent No.2 to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the deceased was aged about 44 years at the time of the accident and he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
To prove the same, produced driving licence (DL) as Ex.P8.

the Tribunal has assessed notional income of deceased as Rs.7,000/-
per month, which is on the lower side.

He further contended in view of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. -v- Pranay Sethi and Others NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB HC-KAR [AIR 2017 SC 5157], 25% of the income of the deceased has to be added for 'future prospects'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. -v- Pranay Sethi and Others NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB HC-KAR [AIR 2017 SC 5157]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: b) Lastly, he has contended that in view of judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. -V- Nanu Ram [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. -V- Nanu Ram [2018 ACJ 2782]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he sought for enhancement of compensation.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel for appearing the Insurance Company has submitted that the even though claimants have claimed that deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month except producing the DL, they have not produced any document to show that he was working as a lorry driver and earning Rs.30,000/-.
Therefore, Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional of the income of the deceased as Rs.7,000/-.

Since the claimants have failed to establish the income of the deceased,
Tribunal has rightly not awarded future NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB HC-KAR prospects.
Finally, he has contended that considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
8.

It is not in dispute that Dundappa died in the road traffic accident occurred on 18.02.2016 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Shift Desire Swift dzire Car bearing No.MH-15/CM-0093 by its driver.

9. Even though the claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month as a driver,
except producing the DL of LMV non transport, claimants have not produced any document to show that the deceased was getting monthly income of Rs.30,000/-, even no bank statement has been produced.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB HC-KAR income of the deceased at Rs.8,750/- per month.

To the aforesaid income, 25% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid Mangala W/O Dundappa @ Gundappa ... vs Swati W/O Subhash Babhulagaonkar And ... on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112153036/
4 down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'Pranay Sethi' (supra) and 1/4th of the income has to be deducted for personal expenses.

entities.text: Mangala W/O Dundappa @ Gundappa ... vs Swati W/O Subhash Babhulagaonkar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.10,937/-.
The deceased was aged about 44 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '14'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.13,78,062/-
(Rs.10,937*12*14*3/4) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
10.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

11. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'Magma General Insurance'
(supra), claimant No.1 is entitled Rs.40,000/- for spousal consortium, claimant Nos. 2 and 3 are entitled Rs.40,000/-
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB HC-KAR each for parental consortium, claimant No.4 and 5 are entitled also Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.

12. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
Compensation under different Amount in (Rs.)

Heads Loss of dependency Rs.13,78,062/-
 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 Spousal consortium Rs.40,000/-
 Parental consortium Rs.80,000/-
 Loss of Filial Rs.80,000/-
 consortium
In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
- 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6564-DB HC-KAR Mangala W/O Dundappa @ Gundappa ... vs Swati W/O Subhash Babhulagaonkar

And ... on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112153036/
5

c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.16,08,062/- as against Rs.9,92,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

d) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
e) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
f) In view of the order dated 16.10.2025 passed by this Court, the claimants are not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 1231 days in filing the appeal.

Sd/-
(H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD) JUDGE Sd/-
